#9659. null becomes mixed on the PHP DTO

I pasted nulls as property values and expected the same type everywhere. On the JSON converter they stay null in the paste, but the drafts diverge. Conversion runs in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.

Laravel writes null for each key. TypeScript types each field as null. The PHP DTO types each property as mixed. CSV writes the headers name,age,meta with an empty row underneath.

That is different from a nested object. When meta is {"active":true}, TypeScript drafts interface Meta and the PHP DTO still uses public array $meta. A null meta does not create that nest. It is mixed on the PHP class and null in TypeScript.

A missing key on the PHP DTO is still assigned with ?? null, including on a property declared public int $id. That is an assignment fallback. A JSON null value is an explicit null in the paste, and the draft types that property as mixed on the PHP class.

The class name stays DataTransferObject. Rename it before the draft ships.

A trailing comma such as {"a":1,} clears every format with Expected double-quoted property name in JSON at position 7 (line 1 column 8). That is not a null. Repair broken text in the JSON formatter, then convert again.

Guide: https://kepttools.com/guides/json-to-typescript-php-dto-laravel

#9657. Claude Code vs Codex vs Gemini CLI vs Hermes: the October 2026 comparison

Posted on Nov 17 • Originally published at colombani.ai • AI-assisted

Codex vs Claude Code vs Gemini CLI? Claude Code suits an engineering team that wants the most built-in controls, Codex an organisation already on ChatGPT, and Gemini CLI a company equipped with Gemini Code Assist. All three read your repository, edit code and run commands.

What is the Google equivalent of Codex? Antigravity CLI for an individual, free with a Google account or included in Google AI Pro and Ultra. In a company, Gemini CLI remains available with a Code Assist licence, a paid API key or Vertex AI.

A command-line (CLI) coding agent reads your repository, edits files and runs commands in your terminal until the task is done.

Four vendors lead the field in October 2026: Anthropic with Claude Code, OpenAI with Codex, Google with Gemini CLI and its consumer successor Antigravity CLI, and NousResearch with Hermes Agent. OpenClaw completes the picture on the community side.

This comparison draws on months of use in real repositories. There is no absolute ranking: the best tool depends on your team, your budget and your data constraints.

Claude Code is our default recommendation for an engineering team: Opus 5.5 on every plan, hooks, skills, per-tool approvals and a classifier-based auto mode. Codex is the natural pick for an organisation already on ChatGPT: it is included in every plan and its code is open. At Google, the answer depends on the account: Antigravity CLI for an individual, Gemini CLI for a company. Hermes Agent suits one person who wants a multi-model agent that learns from their sessions.

Prices come from the vendors' official pages, in US dollars before tax, checked on October 16, 2026.

Rolling out a coding agent to a team? Colombani.ai trains developers on the tool you choose: our Claude Code training, two days on your repositories, or Codex for teams already on ChatGPT.

The facts that changed this comparison since September, checked against the vendors' changelogs and pricing pages.

The verdict rests on repeated use in real repositories rather than a one-shot benchmark. Five criteria matter in production: quality on multi-file changes, context retention, tool integration, team governance and total operating cost.

Every price, version and licence quoted here was checked on October 16, 2026 against the vendor's documentation, GitHub repository or changelog, linked at the end. Colombani.ai trains teams on Claude Code and on Codex, so readers know where the author stands.

All of these agents support MCP (Model Context Protocol), the standard protocol that lets them plug into the same external tools: databases, ticketing, documentation. The real differences lie elsewhere.

Data residency means where your requests are processed and stored. For an organisation subject to GDPR, this row often weighs more than the price.

Claude Code is the oldest CLI agent from a major vendor: its public repository dates from February 2025, two months before those of Codex and Gemini CLI.

Since version 2.1.280 (September 22, 2026), Opus 5.5 is the default model on every plan, including Pro and the Team Standard seat. Opus excels at long tasks: multi-file refactoring, subtle bug hunting, system architecture.

The agentic loop. Claude Code sends a request to the Claude API. The response includes a stop_reason: "tool_use" means the model wants to use a tool (read a file, run a command), "end_turn" means it's done. The model itself decides when to stop.

Agentic search. Anthropic abandoned the RAG approach (vector database) in favor of iterative search: Grep, Glob, Read. The model searches, refines, searches again. Slower than a vector index, but significantly more reliable on real code.

Auto mode uses classifiers that evaluate the risk of each action before executing it. Writing a test file: low risk, automatic execution. Deleting a directory: high risk, asks for confirmation.

The harness, meaning everything around the model that guides and constrains it. CLAUDE.md gives the model persistent context: coding conventions, architecture, business constraints. Since version 2.1.277 (September 18), Claude Code reads AGENTS.md when a repository has no CLAUDE.md. Skills package reusable procedures, and Hooks run a check before or after each action.

Beyond the terminal. Subagents are stable and run in the background. Agent teams, where several instances split a task, remain experimental and off by default. Routines run scheduled tasks in the cloud, and since September 17 Projects coordinate parallel sessions with shared memory.

Opus is not the top of the range. Anthropic also offers Fable, available in Claude Code through the best alias, with its own weekly limit and, depending on the plan, usage credits.

The downsides. Claude Code is not open source and has no free plan. The one million token context window is now standard on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, so the old context limitation is gone.

Codex is OpenAI's agent, written in Rust. Its code has been published under the Apache 2.0 licence since the first commit on April 16, 2025. This permissive licence allows commercial use, modification and redistribution, and expressly grants a patent licence.

Built into ChatGPT. Since July 9, 2026 (version 26.707), Codex is part of the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS and Windows. For an organisation already on ChatGPT Business or Enterprise, the coding agent is available without a new contract.

The models. GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6 Sol arrived on September 22, 2026, and GPT-6.1 Sol on September 29. GPT-5.5 was retired on October 14 for users signed in with their ChatGPT account. Sessions authenticated with an API key are not affected.

What each plan gives you. Free and Go ($8) open Codex in the desktop app with GPT-6 Luna. The CLI, the IDE extension and Codex on the web are available from the Plus plan ($20), with GPT-6.1 Sol. Pro comes at $100, $200 and $500, Business costs $20 per user billed annually or $25 monthly, and Enterprise and Edu are priced on request.

Native subagents and fast startup. Codex delegates subtasks to parallel agents. Charlie Marsh, the author of uv and ruff, rewrote its startup phase on August 20, which is now about 25 times faster. Amazon Bedrock is natively supported as a provider, useful when code must stay on infrastructure you control.

The downsides. The codex mcp-server command, which exposed Codex as an MCP server to other tools, was removed on September 5, 2026: integrations that used it must move to the app server. Usage limits depend on the plan and the model, and are best measured on the usage dashboard rather than the price list.

This question comes up constantly, and the two tools have converged: repository access, MCP, skills, subagents, hooks. Comparing their features is no longer enough to tell them apart. Three questions settle it.

Which subscription does the organisation already pay for? A company on ChatGPT Business gets Codex at no extra cost. A company on Claude Team gets Claude Code from the Standard seat. The entry price is the same: $20 a month billed annually.

What does it need to be able to verify? Codex publishes its harness code under Apache 2.0, which makes it auditable. Claude Code keeps a readable local record of what the agent saw and sent, with tool-by-tool approvals.

Who reviews the code it produces? For a team shipping to production, Claude Code with Opus 5.5 remains our default recommendation. Codex takes the lead when internal policy requires an open licence or routing through Amazon Bedrock.

The two combine well: one agent writes, the other reviews, and their blind spots differ. The detailed analysis is in Codex or Claude Code: how to choose in 2026.

For an individual: Antigravity CLI. Available to everyone, it shares its engine with Antigravity 2.0, Google's desktop app for agent-first development. It is written in Go and orchestrates several agents in the background. It keeps Gemini CLI's key features: Skills, Hooks, subagents and extensions, now called plugins.

For a company: Gemini CLI remains available. Organisations with a Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licence keep their access, as do paid API keys and Vertex AI. Version 0.64.0 (October 13, 2026) runs on the Gemini 3 family, with Gemini 3.1 Pro in preview. The repository README states that Gemini CLI has not been optimized for Gemini 4 Argon and points to Antigravity for that model.

What sets them apart. Gemini CLI stays open source under Apache 2.0. The Antigravity CLI repository only publishes documentation and the changelog. Antigravity CLI, on the other hand, offers Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 to authorised Google Cloud projects. Its auto mode sends any command that would leave the sandbox to a second agent for review.

What is no longer true. Gemini CLI is no longer "free with a Google account". The repository README now says so at the top: for the unpaid tier and Google One users, Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026. Gemini CLI also has Skills, Hooks and subagents, contrary to what this comparison stated before October. Gemini Code Assist for GitHub has accepted no new installations since June 18, except through Google Cloud.

Antigravity CLI's free-tier quotas do not appear in the sources we checked, so we do not quote them. For Gemini on the productivity side, see Gemini for business.

Hermes Agent from NousResearch is the most original on this list. Its standout feature: a built-in learning loop. The agent creates skills from your sessions, improves them through use, and builds a persistent profile of your preferences.

NousResearch describes it as the only agent with a built-in learning loop: it adapts to its user automatically, where Claude Code requires maintaining a CLAUDE.md file by hand.

Multi-provider. Hermes works with OpenRouter, Nous Portal, OpenAI, your own endpoint or local models, and can switch models mid-session. Since 0.22.0, it installs llama.cpp and runs an open model on your machine in one click, with no account and no API key.

Multi-platform. Beyond the terminal, Hermes can be driven from a desktop app, Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp or Signal, through a single gateway.

A project that has grown considerably. Six months after its first public releases in March 2026, Hermes has around 254,000 GitHub stars as of October 16, under the MIT licence. The 0.22.0 cycle alone brought together about 2,500 contributors. Version 0.22.2 (October 15) is the latest stable release.

The downsides. The pace is still dizzying: about 24,000 commits between 0.21.0 and 0.22.0. The stable release channels introduced on October 14 reduce the risk, but pinning a version remains the rule before any client work. The learning loop can retain mistakes. And the optional GODMODE skill, which ships sample prompts for bypassing guardrails, raises a legitimate security question.

Codex is a software vendor's coding agent, tied to a ChatGPT subscription and to OpenAI models. Hermes is a provider-independent personal agent that also writes code.

Choose Codex when the agent serves a team that must share configuration, billing and administration: ChatGPT workspace, SSO, audit logs, residency controls on Enterprise.

Choose Hermes when one person wants a single agent for code, messaging and scheduled tasks, with the model of their choice, including a local one. The hermes import-agent command, added in August, imports an existing Codex or Claude Code setup.

Both licences are permissive: Apache 2.0 for Codex, MIT for Hermes. The difference is governance: Codex is administered like an enterprise service, while Hermes is self-hosted and secured by its user.

OpenClaw (ex-Clawdbot, ex-Moltbot) has the most chaotic trajectory of the bunch: renamed twice after an Anthropic trademark complaint, 60,000 GitHub stars in 72 hours at launch, around 392,000 as of October 16, 2026, and its creator, Peter Steinberger, hired by OpenAI.

Persistent local memory. This feature is what made it a success. OpenClaw remembers your sessions for weeks, with no configuration.

Works with several models. It runs with Claude, GPT or open models such as Kimi.

More than a coding agent. OpenClaw positions itself as a "Life OS": WhatsApp connection, calendar management, third-party app control. The most ambitious approach, and the riskiest.

The downsides. Security. 923 OpenClaw gateways were recorded as exposed without authentication, with shell access and API keys in plain text. If you deploy OpenClaw, lock it down before any use: our AI agent security course covers isolation, permissions and exfiltration through agent tools.

GitHub Copilot CLI requires an active Copilot subscription and can be disabled by the organisation's administrator (version 1.0.99, October 16). OpenCode is an open source, multi-model agent under the MIT licence, with around 214,000 stars (version 1.19.1, October 15). Amp runs its agents remotely: they keep working after you close your laptop. Cursor CLI brings Cursor's agent to the terminal, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Cursor.

Already deploying agents in production? Beyond the tool, two turnkey offerings:

Here are our recommendations by use case.

Demanding solo developer: Claude Code. Opus 5.5 by default from the Pro plan makes the difference when every mistake costs you time. Alternative: Antigravity CLI to get started with a Google account.

Structured engineering team: Claude Code. Shared CLAUDE.md in Git, Hooks to enforce conventions, worktrees for parallel work. The investment in the harness pays off once the team exceeds two or three people.

Organisation already on ChatGPT Business or Enterprise: Codex. The agent is included, so is the administration, and the Apache 2.0 licence makes the harness auditable.

Company on Google Cloud: Gemini CLI with a Code Assist licence, or Antigravity CLI attached to your Google Cloud projects.

Enterprise or mid-size company: Claude Code. Governance (Skills, security Hooks, permissions) and the tool's track record meet the requirements of structured teams. Before a company-wide rollout, an enterprise AI maturity audit shows what can be tested now and what must be prepared.

Team building its own agents: once the coding agent is mastered, the MCP and Agent SDK training teaches how to design, evaluate and run custom agents, with their MCP servers. Architects who want that skill attested can follow our preparation for the Claude Certified Architect certification, issued by Anthropic.

Student or learner: Antigravity CLI with a Google account, or Codex in the ChatGPT app from the free plan.

Open source contributor: Codex, Gemini CLI, Hermes Agent or OpenCode, all published under open licences.

Multi-model experimentation: Hermes Agent. Mid-session model switching and one-click local models make it easy to compare LLMs on the same project.

Power user: OpenClaw. Persistent memory and the multi-platform approach are unique. Secure your installation.

Business teams who do not code: these command-line agents are not the right entry point; the AI agents training for companies runs on the tool already in place, with no terminal; for an organisation on ChatGPT, the ChatGPT training for companies follows the same approach.

To roll out one of these agents to a team, Colombani.ai offers two courses: Claude Code in production and Codex.

At Colombani.ai, we train first on Claude Code, because it brings together the most complete set of tools: CLAUDE.md, Skills, Hooks, per-tool approvals and a classifier-based auto mode. We also train on Codex for teams that work in ChatGPT.

Every training shows the alternatives, because methodology matters as much as the tool. Structuring your context, planning before coding, verifying systematically: these principles work with any agent.

A well-written CLAUDE.md is a project conventions document, and Claude Code now reads AGENTS.md, the format Codex also uses. Skills exist at Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. The discipline of verification (tests, diff review) is universal.

The field moves fast: Google replaced its consumer agent within a month, OpenAI changed models twice in one week, and Hermes passed 250,000 stars in six months. A structured method for coding with AI keeps all its value.

Once the tool is chosen, the Claude Code in production or Codex course gets your team to adopt the method, on your own repositories.

Ulysse Trin is the founder of Colombani.ai, an AI consulting and training firm based in Paris. This article first appeared on the Colombani.ai blog.

#9656. Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run

Hugging Face and OpenRouter are teaming up to make open-weight models easy to run. Every major open-weight release is already being published on the Hugging Face Hub, and OpenRouter serves those models at scale, routing each request across 80+ providers based on live measurements of each one. Together, every open-weight model on the Hub that a provider serves can be called with your Hugging Face token, through the same API, with the best provider picked for each request.

Today, we are switching Inference Providers from our own custom router to OpenRouter's. Requests made to language models now go through OpenRouter, which picks the best provider for each call based on live price, speed and reliability, and retries on another provider if the first one fails. Your code stays the same.

The router supports OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs and Anthropic's Messages API for every chat model, whatever the provider behind it. Pick your coding agent or SDK and a model, then copy the steps, or copy the whole setup as a prompt for your agent:

Setup guides for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and Hermes Agent

The same Hugging Face token also gives you storage with Storage Buckets, compute with Jobs and dedicated inference with Inference Endpoints. PRO, Team and Enterprise plans include monthly credits for compute and inference.

On OpenRouter, open-weight models went from 26.8% of the tokens served in October 2025 to 71.7% at the end of September 2026, after peaking at 77.5% in July (OpenRouter, October 2026). Over the same period, weekly open-weight volume grew more than 60-fold, against almost tenfold for closed models. This week, the most used model on OpenRouter is an open-weight one, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, with 59.2 trillion tokens (rankings).

Open-weight models cost about four times less on average: $0.28 per million input tokens and $1.62 per million output tokens, against $1.27 and $6.36 for closed models.

The best open-weight models still trail the best proprietary ones on the hardest benchmarks. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Kimi K3.1 Pro, the best open-weight model, scores 46 against 65 for Claude Fable 5.2, at about a seventh of the cost per task ($3.68 against $26.54). For a lot of workloads, that trade-off is worth it.

OpenRouter serves more than 800 trillion tokens a month to over 10 million users, across 600+ models from 80+ providers. Its routing is based on live measurements of every provider across that traffic.

OpenRouter recently rebuilt its provider routing: instead of only looking at the lowest list price, it sends each request to the provider with the best mix of price, speed and reliability.

When a provider slows down or starts failing, traffic moves away from it until it recovers, and a failed try is retried on the next best provider inside the same call. In OpenRouter's measurements, the new routing cut capacity errors by 46% and improved time to first token by 16.9% and throughput by 16.3%.

Before, Inference Providers picked one provider for your request and returned its error if it failed. Now, the request is retried on another provider. You can still choose a policy or a provider with a suffix on the model id:

Routing is also cache-aware: a conversation stays on the provider that holds its prompt cache. To make it explicit, send a stable UUID per conversation in the X-HF-Session-Id header (see the prompt caching guide).

Pricing doesn't change: you pay the provider's price on your Hugging Face bill, and Hugging Face doesn't add a markup on top of it. PRO users get $2 of credits every month, and Team and Enterprise organizations get $2 per seat. See Pricing and Billing for the details.

Image, video, and audio generation continue to work exactly as before, directly through Hugging Face Inference Providers without going through OpenRouter. You can keep using the same token and API, and access tens of thousands of LoRAs.

On model pages, you can chat with the model right away in the widget. Two new tabs show what's behind it: Providers lists every provider OpenRouter can route the model to, with its input and output price, speed and uptime over the last 24 hours, and Metrics shows the best price, throughput, time to first token, context length and uptime among them:

Your usage overview breaks your spend down by the provider each request went to:

In your settings, you can turn off any provider you don't want: the router never sends your requests there. Organizations have the same settings, and they apply to every request billed to the organization.

Requests to language models now go through OpenRouter and are billed to your Hugging Face account or organization, so you can no longer use your own API key for a provider with these models. You can still pick a provider with a suffix on the model id (model:provider) or turn providers off in your settings, and your code stays the same. Custom keys for image and video providers keep working.

Try a model, or read the Inference Providers docs to get started.

#9654. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.

#9653. How to Ask Wabi to Build the Mini-App You Actually Want: A 4-Part Prompt Formula

I'm the author of Wabi Wiki, an unofficial guide to the Wabi AI assistant — not affiliated with Wabi. The examples below come from the guide's prompts library.

Wabi's party trick is simple to describe and easy to get wrong: you describe what you want in plain language, and it builds a small app inside your chat — a poll, a tracker, a shared list, a quiz. But because Wabi generates each app fresh from your description, a vague request gives you a vague app. After collecting the prompts that work best, the pattern comes down to four parts.

"Build a poll" beats "plan my whole wedding." Wabi does best when each message asks for one thing: one poll, one tracker, one list. If your request has three jobs in it, split it into three messages. You will get three working tools instead of one confused one.

Wabi's specialty is group apps, so name the people. "Make a poll so our group can vote on one of these five movies for Friday night" works because it says who votes and what they are choosing. "Quiz my daughter on Japanese vocabulary for 10 minutes, three times a week" works because it names the person, the subject, the length and the schedule. A request with no audience gets a generic app; a request with a named audience gets one that fits.

If you will check something daily, say so — and ask for a home-screen widget. "Create a countdown to our trip on June 5 and put it on my home screen" tells Wabi both the job and the place. The same goes for check-ins: "Create a habit tracker that fits my morning routine and checks in with me daily" sets the rhythm up front instead of leaving Wabi to guess.

Your first version is a draft, not a verdict. Ask Wabi to add a field, change a reminder time, or share the app with the thread. Each small fix keeps everything that already worked. Starting over from scratch throws away the good parts along with the bad.

Each better version follows the formula: one tool, named people, a place or rhythm, and room to refine.

Pick one small job — a shared list, a poll, a tracker — and write the request with all four parts before you send it. If the result is close but not right, change one thing and ask again. You can find the full prompts library with copy-paste examples for trips, family, health and daily life at Wabi Wiki.

#9652. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9651. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

#9650. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers

Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and company-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

Transfer potatoes to a serving bowl and season with more pepper. Top with chives and enjoy!

#9648. Crypto ETFs: Bringing Centralization Back to Crypto?

The whole point of cryptocurrencies is to offer a decentralized alternative to traditional financial infrastructure with middlemen. In this way, costs and risks, such as blockages and censorship, are reduced. And yet, here we are again, with digital assets reentering the traditional financial world in the form of Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs).

An ETF is an investment vehicle whose shares trade on a stock exchange. In other words, it’s an asset that represents something else without direct exposure —in this case, cryptocurrencies. Spot products hold the underlying crypto, while futures products use contracts linked to its price.

So far, coins like Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), and Ripple (XRP) have their own ETF products available for investors. There’s a lot of money in there, too. According to CoinStats, crypto ETFs have over $171 billion of Assets Under Management (AUM).

Such a fact begs the question: is this really beneficial for the want-to-be decentralized crypto world, or is it just a blatant invasion from the old financial system? Let’s explore this topic.

The first thing we must consider is that crypto-related ETFs are not cryptocurrency themselves, in any way, shape, or form. Instead, with a spot ETF, the investor owns shares in a financial product that holds the underlying asset.

That means there’s a company (or another middleman) behind this product, handling all the real coins on your behalf —but you’ll never see the real coins themselves. Future-based products don’t even have third-party coins, and only obtain exposure through financial contracts.

Investing in a crypto ETF isn’t the same as “owning” crypto. You’re basically buying a ticket that represents a certain amount of gold, but it’s not, and it’ll never be, the gold itself. The value of that ticket is completely out of your control, and the middleman who sells these tickets takes a nice cut for handling them. If we think about it in simple terms, that’s it, that’s a crypto ETF.

Well, put that way, it sounds almost like a scam—though, of course, it isn't. There are many people, and especially institutions, that cannot or don’t wish to manage their own "gold" (their own cryptocurrencies). This investment vehicle is a service that offers them greater security and convenience, allowing them to gain some exposure without the major risks. After all, self-custody has its perils, too.

Self-custody requires work and responsibility, while many investors are more familiar with the brokerage environment. They often rely on regulated middlemen to handle sensitive financial transactions, and they’re comfortable within this system. Big companies, especially, aren’t suddenly learning how to properly set up and store a cold wallet with millions of dollars inside. Instead, they’re hiring the services or buying the products of experts in the matter, if they want to add crypto to their portfolios.

Therefore, trust is something ETFs can bring to the crypto world. And regulated trust is what institutions are usually looking for. Institutional participation can bring more liquidity (always a good thing) and connect crypto markets with traditional finance. The scale of recent inflows shows that these products have become an important bridge between the two worlds. As described by CoinStats, there was an inflow of over $5.2 billion to crypto ETFs in August alone.

Regulated investment products like ETFs introduce disclosure, reporting, and oversight requirements that many crypto platforms have historically lacked, so that’s why institutions may prefer them over self-custody. Access can be easier too, since you can buy through a traditional brokerage account. Someone else is responsible for every difficult part, and you just handle your investment. It’s fast and not cheap, but convenient.

Convenience is not synonymous with security—not by a long shot. Exchanges can be hacked or go bankrupt. The same can happen to other custodians, such as the firms behind ETFs. But beyond that lies the risk of the crypto industry’s sudden centralization. As we’ve mentioned above, crypto ETFs have over $171 billion AUM. That’s barely 6.5% of the whole cryptocurrency market cap… for now. We need to check the potential rise of these figures, too.

Since their inception in 2024, that same percentage has been growing. As we can see from CMC data, the AUM as a percentage of market cap started at 2.6% in 2024. Then, it was 5.8% in 2025, and now here we are. If they keep up like this, their average growth rate would be around 1.9% per year.

Does this mean ETFs and the firms behind them will take over most of the crypto industry in some years? It’s highly unlikely. At this rate, they’d need a stagnant crypto market capitalization and at least 23 years to reach 51%. However, it’s still concerning that billions in crypto arepooling towards centralized institutions, which could give them substantial power over decentralized crypto networks.

Especially in Proof-of-Stake (PoS) networks like Ethereum or Cardano, “validators” stake (lock) a certain amount to have the right to approve/reject transactions, partake in governance voting, and receive rewards. The more they stake, the more power they have. In a grim scenario, if an ETF brand decides to stake its billions, it could potentially manipulate entire networks. Smaller networks, with fewer community members and nodes, are the most vulnerable.

Centralization around the rules of a single country may also be possible, given that ETFs are products regulated according to their region. Currently, according to ETFLlama, the vast majority (144) are domiciled in Switzerland, followed by the US (76) and the EU (59). However, measured by Assets Under Management (AUM), the leaders are the US ($114.7 billion), Switzerland ($5.53 billion), and the UK ($5.36 billion).

A current reality is that ETFs have to comply with their country's laws, and that could mean censorship for certain users of PoS networks. For instance, for those listed by OFAC in the US. The fact is that the presence of big, powerful players always entails risks, and cryptocurrencies were created precisely to avoid those risks.

Crypto ETFs show how far digital assets have moved into traditional finance. They make access easier and attract institutional money, but every layer of intermediation can also concentrate control. That matters because decentralization is more than a technical feature.

It’s about keeping control distributed, reducing dependence on institutions, and preserving the ability to transact without asking a financial intermediary for permission. Obyte, for instance, takes this idea further by using a DAG-based network without miners or “validators”. There are no block producers deciding which transactions enter the ledger, creating a different model for distributing control across the network.

Now, ETFs can coexist with decentralized cryptocurrencies, and they can bring useful access to people who prefer traditional financial products. Yet the more crypto moves through centralized gateways, the more important its underlying decentralized infrastructure becomes. For projects like Obyte, maintaining that decentralization is part of the point itself. It keeps the original idea of crypto alive: giving users more direct control over their digital assets and transactions.

So, the ideal approach is to strike a balance. We can perfectly well coexist with the traditional financial system and benefit mutually, while remembering why cryptocurrencies exist in the first place and choosing those that are best for the job. After all, self-custody and direct, disintermediated control are the only things that grant us freedom and ownership.

What's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Your net worth is the single most important number in personal finance. Not your salary. Not your credit score. Not how much you have in checking. Your net worth — the gap between everything you own and everything you owe — tells you exactly where you stand financially and whether you are moving in the right direction.

Net Worth = Total Assets - Total Liabilities

That is it. Add up everything you own that has monetary value. Subtract everything you owe. The number that remains — positive or negative — is your net worth.

In the FI community, net worth is not just a number. It is the scoreboard. Your FI number (25 times your annual spending) is a net worth target. Every dollar you save and invest moves you closer. Every dollar of debt you pay off does the same. Tracking your net worth turns the abstract concept of "financial independence" into a concrete, measurable goal.

Let's walk through exactly how to calculate yours, what counts as an asset, what counts as a liability, and how to use this number to accelerate your path to FI.

Calculating your net worth requires two lists: everything you own (assets) and everything you owe (liabilities). The difference between these two numbers is your net worth.

An asset is anything you own that has monetary value. Be honest and conservative — list items at what they would actually sell for today, not what you paid for them or what you hope they are worth.

A note on your home: The FI community debates whether to include your primary residence in net worth calculations. The pragmatic approach is to include it but recognize it is an illiquid asset that does not generate income. For FI planning purposes, many people track two numbers: total net worth (including home equity) and investable net worth (excluding home equity). Your investable net worth is what actually funds your financial independence.

A liability is any debt or financial obligation you owe to someone else.

A surgeon earning $400,000 per year with $600,000 in student loans, a $1.2 million mortgage, and $50,000 in car loans might have a lower net worth than a teacher earning $55,000 who has been investing 30% of her salary into index funds for 15 years. Income is what flows in. Net worth is what you keep. The FI community learned this lesson early: it is not about how much you earn — it is about the gap between earning and spending, compounded over time.

Let's walk through a real example. Meet Sarah, a 32-year-old software developer earning $95,000 per year. She has been saving and investing for 5 years since paying off her credit cards.

Sarah's net worth is $140,700. If her annual spending is $45,000, her FI number is $1,125,000 (25 x $45,000). She is 12.5% of the way there. More importantly, she is tracking her number every month and watching it grow — which means she can project when she will reach FI and make strategic decisions about how to accelerate the timeline.

Her investable net worth (excluding the car, which depreciates) is $155,200 - $30,500 = $124,700 in productive financial assets. This is the number that matters most for FI planning.

A negative net worth means you owe more than you own. This is completely normal — and far more common than people realize. According to Federal Reserve data, the median net worth for Americans under 35 is $39,000, but this is skewed by homeowners. For young renters with student loans, a negative net worth in the range of -$20,000 to -$80,000 is typical.

A negative net worth does not mean you are failing. It means you are early in the journey. If you graduated with $80,000 in student loans and have $5,000 in savings, your net worth is -$75,000. But if you are earning income, paying down debt, and starting to invest, your trajectory is positive — and trajectory is what matters.

The FI community is full of people who started with six-figure negative net worths and reached financial independence in 10-15 years. The key was tracking the number, seeing the progress, and letting that momentum fuel consistent action.

Calculating your net worth once is useful. Tracking it monthly is transformational. Monthly tracking turns financial independence from an abstract goal into a visible, measurable trajectory.

The FI community's favorite: Many FI practitioners use a simple spreadsheet. Create columns for each account, update balances on the first of every month, and chart the total over time. The visual of a steadily rising line graph is one of the most powerful motivators on the FI path. Some people prefer Empower for automated tracking — it links to your accounts and updates your net worth in real time.

Your net worth will not increase in a straight line. Market drops will temporarily reduce your investment balances. Large purchases (a car, a home down payment) will create short-term dips. The number to watch is the 12-month trend. If your net worth is higher than it was a year ago, you are moving in the right direction.

Early in the journey, debt payoff drives most of the growth. A $30,000 student loan shrinking to $18,000 adds $12,000 to your net worth just as effectively as saving $12,000 in new investments. Later, compound growth takes over and your net worth starts increasing faster than your contributions — that is the magic inflection point where your money starts working harder than you do.

Use these calculators to see where you stand on your FI journey.

Find out how much you need to reach financial independence.

See if your current investments can coast to your retirement target.

Your savings rate matters more than returns. See where you are.

Complete this in one sitting — it takes about 30 minutes.

Log into every bank account, retirement account, brokerage account, and HSA. Write down the current balance. For your home, use Zillow's estimate minus 10%. For vehicles, use Kelley Blue Book private party value.

Pro tip: Do not include personal belongings like furniture, clothing, or electronics unless a single item is worth more than $1,000 at resale.

Log into every loan servicer, credit card account, and any other creditor. Write down the exact payoff balance — not the monthly payment, but the total remaining balance including any accrued interest.

Total assets minus total liabilities equals your net worth. Whether this number is positive, negative, or zero, write it down. This is your starting point.

Multiply your annual spending by 25. This is how much investable net worth you need to be financially independent using the 4% safe withdrawal rate. Divide your current investable net worth by your FI number to see your progress percentage.

Pro tip: Use your actual spending, not your income. If you earn $80,000 but spend $50,000, your FI number is $1,250,000 — not $2,000,000.

Choose a tool — Empower, a spreadsheet, or a notebook — and schedule a recurring monthly reminder to update your net worth. The first of each month works well. Track the number, chart the trend, and watch your progress compound.

The most common habit among people who have reached financial independence is consistent net worth tracking. It takes 5 minutes per month and creates a feedback loop that keeps you motivated and accountable. When you see your net worth climb from $50,000 to $100,000 to $250,000, the progress becomes its own fuel. Start tracking today — your future self will thank you.

Yes, but with context. Your home is an asset and your mortgage is a liability, so both should be included for an accurate net worth picture. However, for FI planning, track your investable net worth (excluding home equity) separately — because you cannot live off your home equity unless you sell or take a reverse mortgage. Many FI practitioners track both numbers.

Monthly is the sweet spot for most people. Weekly is too frequent and causes unnecessary anxiety about market fluctuations. Quarterly is too infrequent to maintain the motivational feedback loop. Set a recurring reminder on the first of each month, update your numbers in 5 minutes, and move on.

The median net worth by age (from Federal Reserve SCF data): under 35 is $39,000, 35-44 is $135,600, 45-54 is $247,200, 55-64 is $364,500, 65-74 is $409,900. FI community members typically far exceed these benchmarks because they prioritize saving and investing. See our average net worth by age guide for detailed breakdowns.

Yes. Your 401(k), IRA, Roth IRA, 403(b), TSP, and any other retirement accounts are assets and should be included in your net worth calculation. Some people adjust for taxes (since traditional 401(k) withdrawals are taxed as income), but for tracking purposes, including the full balance is standard practice.

A negative net worth simply means you owe more than you own — it is common for recent graduates, new homeowners, and anyone early in their career. What matters is the direction. If your net worth is -$50,000 but was -$65,000 a year ago, you are making significant progress. Focus on the trajectory, not the absolute number.

Yes, include your car at its current resale value (Kelley Blue Book private party value, not dealer retail). Cars are depreciating assets, which means their value decreases over time, but they still have monetary value and should be counted. If you have an auto loan, both the car (asset) and the loan balance (liability) should appear in your calculation.

Calculating your net worth is the first step on the path to financial independence — and it takes less than 30 minutes. Add up everything you own, subtract everything you owe, and you have the single most important number in your financial life. Whether that number is positive, negative, or zero, it is your starting point. Track it monthly, watch it grow, and use it to measure your progress toward your FI number. The formula is simple: assets minus liabilities. The habit of tracking it is what separates people who talk about financial goals from people who achieve them.

#9641. Turkey Cheese Ball

The turkey may be the main event of Thanksgiving dinner, but it can be a snack, too! Whether you're hosting Thanksgiving for your community or celebrating with family, this fun appetizer is the perfect way to get everyone excited for the big turkey dinner with another smaller turkey! This cheese ball is not only the most eye-catching appetizer you can add to your holiday menu, but it’s surprisingly easy to create.

What People Are Saying:“I made this for Friendsgiving. It was delicious and I got several comments on how great it tasted.” - kellykcox34580

In a food processor, pulse the cream cheese, goat cheese, butter, and garlic powder until the mixture is smooth. Add parsley, chives, and thyme and pulse until well combined. Then season with salt and black pepper.

Transfer the cream cheese mixture to a piece of plastic wrap and gather up the wrap to form a ball. Then transfer the mixture into a large bowl and refrigerate until it’s firm, which should take at least three hours and up to one day.

In a clean food processor, pulse 3/4 cup pecan halves until they are finely chopped.

Roll the cheese ball in nuts and arrange it all on a platter.

Start by cutting a large triangle from a red bell pepper—this will be the face. Next, cut a smaller triangle from a yellow bell pepper for the beak. For the eyes, slice two small rounds from a small carrot. Take a larger carrot and slice it into diagonal ovals to make the feet, then carve little triangles at one end to look like toes. Finally, thinly slice the rest of the carrots into matchsticks for the tail.

Grab some toothpicks and stick the carrot eyes onto the red triangle face. Then, use another toothpick to add the yellow beak to the face—just make sure all the toothpicks point toward the back so you can attach everything to the cheese ball later. Now, press the face onto the front of the cheese ball, and slide the carrot feet into the base.

Insert matchstick carrots, pretzel sticks, and mini pretzels into the back of the ball to create the tail. Using the remaining 1/2 cup pecan halves, create wings by overlapping them along each side of the ball. Serve with crackers alongside!

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Store leftover cheese ball in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. If possible, remove the pretzels and vegetable decorations before storing, as they can soften over time.

#9640. Poulet Basquaise

Rich tomatoes, stewed onions and peppers, and tender bone-in chicken make this Spanish- and French-inspired poulet Basquaise recipe extremely flavorful while still being surprisingly easy to make. Savory and rustic, it’s a stew that’s ideal for making ahead and enjoying all week long. The key ingredient? Piment d’Espelette—the regional spice known for its peppery, smoky essence. If you’re looking to master a classic dish or simply want a reliable, cozy weeknight dinner, then this recipe won’t let you down.

Heat a large skillet with oil and season the chicken with salt. Working in batches, add the chicken pieces and sear until the skin is golden in color, which should take 5 to 7 minutes. Remove the chicken to a heatproof plate.

Then reduce the heat and add the onion, bell peppers, garlic, piment d’Espelette, and salt. You’ll want to stir this once in a while so it doesn’t stick, but also let the vegetables soften. This should take 8 to 10 minutes.

At this point, increase the heat again and add the wine. Scrape up any bits on the bottom and allow those peppers and onions to absorb the wine. The liquid should reduce.

Add the tomatoes and broth and bring to a simmer. Be careful of splattering sauce and adjust the heat as needed. Place the chicken back into the skillet, skin side up, and cook until the chicken is tender and nearly falling off the bone. The sauce should also be thicker and fragrant. This should take about 30 to 40 minutes.

Stir in the chorizo and cook until it’s warmed through. Top it off with thyme and serve!

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Let cool and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. It’s certainly a great meal-prep dish. Make this on a Sunday night for lunch Monday and Tuesday.

#9639. Whole Wheat vs. Sourdough: Which Bread Is Healthier?

How to pick the loaf that fits your life.

Whole wheat bread used to be the gold standard of quick, healthy carbs. Unlike white bread, it uses flour milled from the entire wheat kernel, providing extra fiber and vitamins. But sourdough has exploded in popularity over the past decade, offering a seemingly more natural option made from just sourdough starter, flour, and water. Is this ancient breadmaking method healthier than whole wheat, even if it uses white flour?

As a dietitian, I see this showdown between whole wheat and sourdough all the time. People wonder if the rustic, tangy charm of sourdough beats the wholesome, fiber-packed power of whole wheat. Let’s slice into the details and figure out which loaf deserves a spot on your counter.

Whole wheat is exactly what it sounds like. This bread is made using flour from the entire wheat kernel—the bran, germ, and endosperm. Here’s what that means:

Because it includes all parts of the kernel, 100% whole wheat bread delivers fiber, essential vitamins like folate and niacin, and important minerals such as iron and magnesium. That fiber helps you feel satisfied after eating, supports digestion, and can support blood sugar management and heart health. This combination makes this particular bread a smart, nutrient-dense choice for everyday eating.

It’s a reliable, widely available, research-backed whole grain—and most Americans don’t eat the recommended servings of whole grains every day, which the USDA suggests is more than half of the grains we eat. So, choosing whole-grain bread can help people meet this recommendation.

It seems like everyone and their mother got into baking sourdough a few years ago. We all know it’s delicious, but what makes it special from a health perspective isn't just its ingredients—it’s how it is made.

Sourdough isn’t defined by a specific type of flour. You can make it with all-purpose, rye, or whole-wheat flour; some loaves use enriched/fortified flour for an extra boost of iron and B vitamins. And its magic lies in the fermentation process. Instead of commercial yeast, sourdough relies on a “starter,” which is a living mix of wild yeast and beneficial bacteria (specifically, lactobacilli).

This fermentation process does some pretty amazing things:

In a side-by-side battle, let's see which bread comes out on top:

If your primary goal is to maximize your fiber intake and get a consistent, nutrient-packed loaf, 100% whole wheat is an excellent choice.

If you're looking for a bread that’s easier to digest and offers enhanced mineral absorption, deliciously tangy sourdough is your go-to.

But it is possible to have the best of both worlds. Grab (or bake) a sourdough bread made with 100% whole wheat flour for fiber, nutrient density, and fermentation perks.

Whether you’re Team Sourdough or Team Whole Wheat, there’s one universal truth: your body, and let’s be honest, your soul, will thank you. Because we all know that carbs are good for the soul.

#9636. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.

The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.

Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.

You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.

The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)

“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”

“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.

“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”

That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.

If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.

But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”

“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”

In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”

In it, light, airy mashed potatoes are topped with all of the classic baked potato fillings—cheddar cheese, chives, bacon, and sour cream—for a dish that truly embodies the best of both worlds.

The beauty of these potatoes is that they can go with any number of dinners. Serve them alongside your favorite protein—chicken, steak, pork chops, the world is your oyster—or alongside a few lighter sides like any of our green salads, caramelized Brussels sprouts, or roasted green beans.

#9628. What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history.

This article is part of our feature celebrating Pan Dulce. Find all things pan dulce here.

Categorically, piloncillo is a “non-centrifugal” cane sugar, meaning it is an unrefined sugar product and a true natural brown sugar. It’s mostly consumed in Mexico and Latin America, but a similar product can be found in Asia, known as jaggery in India. Though often lumped together, these unrefined dark sugars are very different from brown sugars on the market today, which have been refined to a large degree — in some cases, they’re actually just white sugar with coloring or molasses added.

Making piloncillo, on the other hand, involves an artisanal process that’s hundreds of years old. To make it, pressed cane juice is boiled to evaporate the water and deeply caramelize the sugar. The cooked cane is then poured into molds (often made of wood) and left to dry and harden. Traditional piloncillo is conical in shape and can vary in size from small to large cones but is most commonly found in a medium size that weighs about 200 grams. In Guatemala and Colombia, it is called panela, where it is cooked to a lighter degree and typically formed into a brick, rather than cone, shape. Other forms of piloncillo can be granulated or liquid (which is more rare).

Minimally processed and boldly flavored, piloncillo was historically a prized and respected foodstuff. As an unrefined cane sugar, piloncillo provides more complex vitamins and minerals than refined sugars, which undergo processing and whitening methods that also strip nutrients from the whole food. And piloncillo is also great for baking, providing notes of burnt caramel and hints of smoke. Plus, its rich molasses qualities keep baked goods moist and fresh for longer.

Always look at the ingredient label when purchasing piloncillo and make sure it says 100% pure cane juice or cane sugar. It is becoming increasingly common to find imitation products marketed as jaggery or piloncillo that contain coloring and corn syrup. You can find good piloncillo at specialty grocery stores or online at retailers.

In Mexico and throughout Latin America, piloncillo is an important ingredient in many traditional dishes. (Some will even say it’s not the “real dish” if you substitute sugar in these recipes due to the deep flavors and richness that only piloncillo can provide.) This deep, dark unrefined sugar lends its characteristic flavor and texture to popular foods and beverages such as capirotada, tepache, coyotas, atole, café de olla, calabaza al horno, coricos, and hojarascas, to name a few!

I love adding piloncillo when I’m making champurrado. In this warm and thick chocolate beverage, the piloncillo is chopped or grated and dissolved in the pot with water or milk before adding the chocolate and masa. In this recipe, the piloncillo’s intense sweet and smoky flavors pair well with the chocolate and corn masa.

While there are many dishes and uses for piloncillo, it’s not a simple substitution for granulated white sugar in recipes, but you can use it the same as you would brown sugar with a 1:1 substitution by weight.  Depending on how hard the cone is, it can be crumbled or grated for easier measuring. If it is very hard, try cutting it in half with a sharp knife and then placing it between parchment paper or a towel and beating with a rolling pin.

The cost of a will varies dramatically based on how you create it and how complex your estate is. Here is a comprehensive comparison of every method, from free options to premium attorney packages.

Several factors push will costs toward the higher end of each range:

The will vs trust decision is primarily a financial calculation: does the upfront cost of a trust save more than it costs by avoiding probate?

When you die with only a will (no trust), your estate must go through probate — a court-supervised process where a judge validates your will, your executor inventories assets, debts are paid, and remaining assets are distributed. Probate costs include:

Probate also takes 6-18 months on average and is a public proceeding — anyone can look up your will, your assets, and who inherited what.

A revocable living trust costs $1,500-$5,000 upfront but avoids probate entirely. The math is straightforward:

For most FI-focused households who are building wealth toward financial independence, the trust pays for itself many times over. If your net worth exceeds $100,000-$200,000 and you own real estate, a trust is almost certainly the better financial decision.

Even with a trust, you still need a pour-over will — a short document that catches any assets not transferred into the trust during your lifetime and directs them into the trust at death. You also still need a healthcare directive and durable power of attorney. Most estate plan packages include all four documents together.

The sticker price of a will is only part of the total cost of estate planning. Several hidden costs catch people off guard:

The FI-optimized approach to estate planning minimizes cost without sacrificing protection:

Start with an online will now. A $159 Trust & Will plan gives you a will, healthcare directive, and power of attorney today. Do not let perfect be the enemy of done — having a basic will is infinitely better than having no will while you save up for an attorney.

Upgrade to a trust when your net worth exceeds $200,000. At this point, the probate avoidance savings justify the $1,500-$3,500 cost of adding a trust.

Shop attorney fees aggressively. Estate planning is a competitive market. Get quotes from at least three attorneys. Many offer flat-fee packages, and prices can vary by 50-100% for the same work in the same city. Ask specifically whether the quote includes trust funding assistance and deed transfers.

Use online services for updates. Rather than paying an attorney $200-$500 for a codicil, many online platforms let you update your will for free or for a small annual subscription ($19-$39/year). Trust & Will, for example, includes one year of free updates.

Bundle documents. An estate plan package (will + trust + POA + healthcare directive) typically costs 20-40% less than purchasing each document separately. If you are going to see an attorney, get everything done in one engagement.

Here is the counterintuitive truth: the most expensive estate plan is the one you never create. Dying without a will (intestate) triggers state default rules that may not match your wishes, longer and more expensive probate proceedings, and potential family conflict. For parents of minor children, it means a judge — not you — decides who raises your kids. The $0-$259 cost of an online will is trivially small compared to these consequences.
